{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081344Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/.claude/skills/testing\n\n# Smart Contract Testing\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**You test getters and trivial functions.** Testing that `name()` returns the name is worthless. Test edge cases, failure modes, and economic invariants — the things that lose money when they break.\n\n**You don't fuzz.** `forge test` finds the bugs you thought of. Fuzzing finds the ones you didn't. If your contract does math, fuzz it. If it handles user input, fuzz it. If it moves value, definitely fuzz it.\n\n**You don't fork-test.** If your contract calls Uniswap, Aave, or any external protocol (verified addresses: `addresses/SKILL.md`), test against their real deployed contracts on a fork. Mocking them hides integration bugs that only appear with real state.\n\n**You write tests that mirror the implementation.** Testing that `deposit(100)` sets `balance[user] = 100` is tautological — you're testing that Solidity assignments work. Test properties: \"after deposit and withdraw, user gets their tokens back.\" Test invariants: \"total deposits always equals contract balance.\"\n\n**You skip invariant testing for stateful protocols.** If your contract has multiple interacting functions that change state over time (vaults, AMMs, lending), you need invariant tests. Unit tests check one path; invariant tests check that properties hold across thousands of random sequences.\n\n---\n\n## Unit Testing with Foundry\n\n### Test File Structure\n\n```solidity\n// test/MyContract.t.sol\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\npragma solidity ^0.8.20;\n\nimport {Test, console} from \"forge-std/Test.sol\";\nimport {MyToken} from \"../src/MyToken.sol\";\n\ncontract MyTokenTest is Test {\n    MyToken public token;\n    address public alice = makeAddr(\"alice\");\n    address public bob = makeAddr(\"bob\");\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MyToken(\"Test\", \"TST\", 1_000_000e18);\n        // Give alice some tokens for testing\n        token.transfer(alice, 10_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferUpdatesBalances() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 1_000e18);\n\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(alice), 9_000e18);\n        assertEq(token.balanceOf(bob), 1_000e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_TransferEmitsEvent() public {\n        vm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);\n        emit Transfer(alice, bob, 500e18);\n\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        token.transfer(bob, 500e18);\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferExceedsBalance() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(bob, 999_999e18); // More than alice has\n    }\n\n    function test_RevertWhen_TransferToZeroAddress() public {\n        vm.prank(alice);\n        vm.expectRevert();\n        token.transfer(address(0), 100e18);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Assertion Patterns\n\n```solidity\n// Equality\nassertEq(actual, expected);\nassertEq(actual, expected, \"descriptive error message\");\n\n// Comparisons\nassertGt(a, b);   // a > b\nassertGe(a, b);   // a >= b\nassertLt(a, b);   // a < b\nassertLe(a, b);   // a <= b\n\n// Approximate equality (for math with rounding)\nassertApproxEqAbs(actual, expected, maxDelta);\nassertApproxEqRel(actual, expected, maxPercentDelta); // in WAD (1e18 = 100%)\n\n// Revert expectations\nvm.expectRevert();                           // Any revert\nvm.expectRevert(\"Insufficient balance\");     // Specific message\nvm.expectRevert(MyContract.CustomError.selector); // Custom error\n\n// Event expectations\nvm.expectEmit(true, true, false, true);      // (topic1, topic2, topic3, data)\nemit MyEvent(expectedArg1, expectedArg2);\n```\n\n### What to Actually Test\n\n```solidity\n// ✅ TEST: Edge cases that lose money\nfunction test_TransferZeroAmount() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferEntireBalance() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferToSelf() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_ApproveOverwrite() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_TransferFromWithExactAllowance() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Access control\nfunction test_RevertWhen_NonOwnerCallsAdminFunction() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_OwnerCanPause() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ✅ TEST: Failure modes\nfunction test_RevertWhen_DepositZero() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_WithdrawMoreThanDeposited() public { /* ... */ }\nfunction test_RevertWhen_ContractPaused() public { /* ... */ }\n\n// ❌ DON'T TEST: OpenZeppelin internals\n// function test_NameReturnsName() — they already tested this\n// function test_SymbolReturnsSymbol() — waste of time\n// function test_DecimalsReturns18() — it does, trust it\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fuzz Testing\n\nFoundry automatically fuzzes any test function with parameters. Instead of testing one value, it tests hundreds of random values.\n\n### Basic Fuzz Test\n\n```solidity\n// Foundry calls this with random amounts\nfunction testFuzz_DepositWithdrawRoundtrip(uint256 amount) public {\n    // Bound input to valid range\n    amount = bound(amount, 1, token.balanceOf(alice));\n\n    uint256 balanceBefore = token.balanceOf(alice);\n\n    vm.startPrank(alice);\n    token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n    vault.deposit(amount, alice);\n    vault.withdraw(vault.balanceOf(alice), alice, alice);\n    vm.stopPrank();\n\n    // Property: user gets back what they deposited (minus any fees)\n    assertGe(token.balanceOf(alice), balanceBefore - 1); // Allow 1 wei rounding\n}\n```\n\n### Bounding Inputs\n\n```solidity\n// bound() is preferred over vm.assume() — bound reshapes, assume discards\nfunction testFuzz_Fee(uint256 amount, uint256 feeBps) public {\n    amount = bound(amount, 1e6, 1e30);       // Reasonable token amounts\n    feeBps = bound(feeBps, 1, 10_000);       // 0.01% to 100%\n\n    uint256 fee = (amount * feeBps) / 10_000;\n    uint256 afterFee = amount - fee;\n\n    // Property: fee + remainder always equals original\n    assertEq(fee + afterFee, amount);\n}\n\n// vm.assume() discards inputs — use sparingly\nfunction testFuzz_Division(uint256 a, uint256 b) public {\n    vm.assume(b > 0); // Skip zero (would revert)\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Run with More Iterations\n\n```bash\n# Default: 256 runs\nforge test\n\n# More thorough: 10,000 runs\nforge test --fuzz-runs 10000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml for CI\n# [fuzz]\n# runs = 1000\n```\n\n---\n\n## Fork Testing\n\nTest your contract against real deployed protocols on a mainnet fork. This catches integration bugs that mocks can't.\n\n### Basic Fork Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract SwapTest is Test {\n    // Real mainnet addresses — full verified list: addresses/SKILL.md\n    address constant UNISWAP_ROUTER = 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45;\n    address constant WETH = 0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2;\n    address constant USDC = 0xA0b86991c6218b36c1d19D4a2e9Eb0cE3606eB48;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        // Fork mainnet at a specific block for reproducibility\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", 19_000_000);\n    }\n\n    function test_SwapETHForUSDC() public {\n        address user = makeAddr(\"user\");\n        vm.deal(user, 1 ether);\n\n        vm.startPrank(user);\n\n        // Build swap path\n        ISwapRouter.ExactInputSingleParams memory params = ISwapRouter\n            .ExactInputSingleParams({\n                tokenIn: WETH,\n                tokenOut: USDC,\n                fee: 3000,\n                recipient: user,\n                amountIn: 0.1 ether,\n                amountOutMinimum: 0, // In production, NEVER set to 0\n                sqrtPriceLimitX96: 0\n            });\n\n        // Execute swap\n        uint256 amountOut = ISwapRouter(UNISWAP_ROUTER).exactInputSingle{value: 0.1 ether}(params);\n\n        vm.stopPrank();\n\n        // Verify we got USDC back\n        assertGt(amountOut, 0, \"Should receive USDC\");\n        assertGt(IERC20(USDC).balanceOf(user), 0);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### When to Fork-Test\n\n- **Always:** Any contract that calls an external protocol (Uniswap, Aave, Chainlink)\n- **Always:** Any contract that handles tokens with quirks (USDT, fee-on-transfer, rebasing)\n- **Always:** Any contract that reads oracle prices\n- **Never:** Pure logic contracts with no external calls — use unit tests\n\n### Running Fork Tests\n\n```bash\n# Fork from RPC URL\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY\n\n# Fork at specific block (reproducible)\nforge test --fork-url https://eth-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/v2/YOUR_KEY --fork-block-number 19000000\n\n# Set in foundry.toml to avoid CLI flags\n# [rpc_endpoints]\n# mainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n## Invariant Testing\n\nInvariant tests verify that properties hold across thousands of random function call sequences. Essential for stateful protocols.\n\n### What Are Invariants?\n\nInvariants are properties that must ALWAYS be true, no matter what sequence of actions users take:\n\n- \"Total supply equals sum of all balances\" (ERC-20)\n- \"Total deposits equals total shares times share price\" (vault)\n- \"x * y >= k after every swap\" (AMM)\n- \"User can always withdraw what they deposited\" (escrow)\n\n### Basic Invariant Test\n\n```solidity\ncontract VaultInvariantTest is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n    VaultHandler public handler;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        token = new MockERC20(\"Test\", \"TST\", 18);\n        vault = new MyVault(token);\n        handler = new VaultHandler(vault, token);\n\n        // Tell Foundry which contract to call randomly\n        targetContract(address(handler));\n    }\n\n    // This runs after every random sequence\n    function invariant_TotalAssetsMatchesBalance() public view {\n        assertEq(\n            vault.totalAssets(),\n            token.balanceOf(address(vault)),\n            \"Total assets must equal actual balance\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    function invariant_SharePriceNeverZero() public view {\n        if (vault.totalSupply() > 0) {\n            assertGt(vault.convertToAssets(1e18), 0, \"Share price must never be zero\");\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Handler: guided random actions\ncontract VaultHandler is Test {\n    MyVault public vault;\n    IERC20 public token;\n\n    constructor(MyVault _vault, IERC20 _token) {\n        vault = _vault;\n        token = _token;\n    }\n\n    function deposit(uint256 amount) public {\n        amount = bound(amount, 1, 1e24);\n        deal(address(token), msg.sender, amount);\n\n        vm.startPrank(msg.sender);\n        token.approve(address(vault), amount);\n        vault.deposit(amount, msg.sender);\n        vm.stopPrank();\n    }\n\n    function withdraw(uint256 shares) public {\n        uint256 maxShares = vault.balanceOf(msg.sender);\n        if (maxShares == 0) return;\n        shares = bound(shares, 1, maxShares);\n\n        vm.prank(msg.sender);\n        vault.redeem(shares, msg.sender, msg.sender);\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Running Invariant Tests\n\n```bash\n# Default depth (15 calls per sequence, 256 sequences)\nforge test\n\n# Deeper exploration\nforge test --fuzz-runs 1000\n\n# Configure in foundry.toml\n# [invariant]\n# runs = 512\n# depth = 50\n```\n\n---\n\n## What NOT to Test\n\n- **OpenZeppelin internals.** Don't test that `ERC20.transfer` works. It's been audited by dozens of firms and used by thousands of contracts. Test YOUR logic on top of it.\n- **Solidity language features.** Don't test that `require` reverts or that `mapping` stores values. The compiler works.\n- **Every getter.** If `name()` returns the name you passed to the constructor, that's not a test — it's a tautology.\n- **Happy path only.** The happy path probably works. Test the unhappy paths: what happens with zero? Max uint? Unauthorized callers? Reentrancy?\n\n**Focus your testing effort on:** Custom business logic, mathematical operations, integration points with external protocols, access control boundaries, and economic edge cases.\n\n---\n\n## Pre-Deploy Test Checklist\n\n- [ ] All custom logic has unit tests with edge cases\n- [ ] Zero amounts, max uint, empty arrays, self-transfers tested\n- [ ] Access control verified — unauthorized calls revert\n- [ ] Fuzz tests on all mathematical operations (minimum 1000 runs)\n- [ ] Fork tests for every external protocol integration\n- [ ] Invariant tests for stateful protocols (vaults, AMMs, lending)\n- [ ] Events verified with `expectEmit`\n- [ ] Gas snapshots taken with `forge snapshot` to catch regressions\n- [ ] Static analysis with `slither .` — no high/medium findings unaddressed\n- [ ] All tests pass: `forge test -vvv`\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8df734a9-bd87-4a12-8378-0091c8af4975","uuid":"ed52f6de-ee69-4d6d-93d7-91eb361b9eb6","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:13:49.834Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5","id":"msg_011CdSEAGqYG6CC3FsjgmzWw","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012uuHwanR2chj3bpkcYRZPE","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081344Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why all four symptoms are the same bug\n\n## The root cause\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n```\n\nNo block number. That overload forks at **`latest`**. Every CI run — every test contract inside\na run — forks a different block of a chain that never stops moving.\n\nSo the suite has no fixed input. The Chainlink answer and the Uniswap reserves your assertions\ncompare against are not constants you're testing; they're live market data you're re-downloading\neach run. All four symptoms fall out of that one line.\n\n## How each symptom follows\n\n**1. The sudden reds.** Nothing in your repo changed. Mainnet changed. A Chainlink aggregator only\nwrites a new answer when price deviates past its threshold (~0.5% for ETH/USD) or its heartbeat\nexpires — so an asserted price can sit inside a hardcoded band for months and then step outside it\nin one round. Uniswap reserves move on every swap and every LP mint/burn, so any tolerance you\npicked drifts out as liquidity changes. Three tests turned red this morning because the market\ncrossed your thresholds this morning.\n\nThe important consequence: **the four-month green streak was never evidence these tests passed.**\nIt was evidence the market happened to stay in range. The tests have been broken since they were\nwritten; today is just when it surfaced.\n\n**2. The flakiness on re-run.** Same commit, different head. A re-run 10 minutes later forks a\ndifferent block, where the price may be back inside the band or the Chainlink round hasn't rotated\nyet. Two channels feed this:\n\n- *State drift* — the block you land on decides pass/fail.\n- *Failed RPC calls* — see (4). A request that exhausts Foundry's retries surfaces as a test error,\n  not as a network error, so it reads as a flaky failure.\n\nThere's also intra-run inconsistency: `forge test` runs test **contracts** in parallel, each with\nits own `setUp`, so each resolves `latest` independently and they can land on different blocks\nwithin a single invocation. You cannot assume all your tests saw the same chain state even in one\nrun.\n\n**3. The slowdown.** Foundry caches fork RPC responses on disk, keyed by **chain + block number**\n(`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/`). A moving head means a new key every run, so the hit rate\nis **zero, permanently**. Every `SLOAD`, `eth_getCode`, and `eth_call` your tests touch is a live\nnetwork round trip, every time. As you added tests over four months, the per-run RPC call count grew\nmonotonically and none of it was ever amortized. The cache directory grew too — pure disk bloat, no\nreuse.\n\n**4. The 429s.** Direct consequence of (3). Uncached calls per run × parallel test contracts finally\ncrossed your free tier's rate / compute-unit ceiling. And this feeds back: 429 → Foundry backs off\nand retries → longer wall time (worse slowdown) → exhausted retries → test error (more flakiness).\n\nOne line, four symptoms, with a reinforcing loop between the last two.\n\n## The fix\n\n### 1. Pin the block\n\n```toml\n# foundry.toml\n[rpc_endpoints]\nmainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n\n[rpc_storage_caching]\nchains    = [\"mainnet\"]\nendpoints = \"all\"\n```\n\n```solidity\ncontract ForkTest is Test {\n    // Bump deliberately, in its own PR. Never \"latest\".\n    uint256 constant FORK_BLOCK = 19_000_000;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", FORK_BLOCK);\n    }\n}\n```\n\nNow the Chainlink answer and the pool reserves at that block are *constants*. Assert exact values,\nnot tolerance bands — a band is just a slower way to be non-deterministic:\n\n```solidity\nfunction test_ChainlinkPriceAtForkBlock() public view {\n    (, int256 answer,,,) = AggregatorV3Interface(ETH_USD_FEED).latestRoundData();\n    assertEq(answer, 224_351_000_000); // read once at FORK_BLOCK, then frozen\n}\n```\n\nTreat the pin like a lockfile: bumping it is a reviewed change, and if a protocol upgrade breaks\nyou, the diff says so instead of a random Tuesday saying so.\n\n### 2. Split what these tests are actually for\n\nPinning fixes determinism but doesn't fix the design problem: two different questions are being\nanswered by one test.\n\n- *\"Does our integration wire up against the real deployed contracts?\"* → pinned fork test. Correct\n  use, keep it.\n- *\"Does our logic behave correctly across price ranges?\"* → **don't fork at all.** Mock the feed\n  and fuzz the price. A market move should be incapable of turning CI red.\n\n```solidity\nfunction testFuzz_HandlesAnyPrice(int256 price) public {\n    price = int256(bound(uint256(price), 1e8, 100_000e8));\n    vm.mockCall(\n        ETH_USD_FEED,\n        abi.encodeWithSelector(AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData.selector),\n        abi.encode(uint80(1), price, block.timestamp, block.timestamp, uint80(1))\n    );\n    // ... assert your logic, no network involved\n}\n```\n\nThis is also where you should be testing the cases a live fork will basically never hand you:\nstale rounds, a zero or negative answer, a price that moved 40% between two calls.\n\n### 3. Cache the RPC responses in CI\n\nOnce the block is pinned the cache is reusable, so make CI keep it:\n\n```yaml\n- uses: actions/cache@v4\n  with:\n    path: ~/.foundry/cache/rpc\n    key: foundry-rpc-${{ env.FORK_BLOCK }}-${{ hashFiles('test/**/*.sol') }}\n    restore-keys: foundry-rpc-${{ env.FORK_BLOCK }}-\n```\n\nAfter the first warm run, a normal PR makes close to zero RPC calls. That is what actually kills the\n429s and the slowdown — pinning alone only makes the cache *possible*.\n\n### 4. Survive the cold run\n\nThe first run at a new pin still downloads state, in a burst, in parallel. Throttle it:\n\n```bash\nforge test --compute-units-per-second 100   # or --no-rpc-rate-limit if you have headroom\n```\n\n## Does this work against a free-tier endpoint? — plainly\n\n**Pinning to a block older than ~128 blocks requires archive state, and the fix does not work\nwithout it.** That is the one thing your endpoint may not provide.\n\nA full (non-archive) node prunes historical world state after ~128 blocks (~25 minutes). Fork\ntesting at `FORK_BLOCK` needs historical `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getCode`, and\n`eth_call` **at that block**. Outside the window, a non-archive node cannot answer.\n\nFree tiers vary and terms change, so don't take anyone's word for it — including mine. Check yours:\n\n```bash\n# 1. historical state read\ncast balance 0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045 \\\n  --block 19000000 --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\"\n\n# 2. historical eth_call — what fork tests actually need\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestAnswer()(int256)\" \\\n  --block 19000000 --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\"\n```\n\n- Both return values → you have archive at that depth. Ship the fix as written.\n- Either errors with `missing trie node`, `state is not available`,\n  `Historical state not available`, or a bare `-32000` → **no archive**. Note that some providers\n  serve archive but only for a limited lookback, so run the check against the exact block you plan\n  to pin, not an arbitrary old one.\n\nAlso check the ceiling, not just capability: free tiers cap requests/sec and monthly compute units.\nArchive calls are usually billed at a higher weight. A cold run at a fresh pin can burn a\nmeaningful chunk of a monthly free quota in one go.\n\n### If you don't have archive\n\nIn rough order of preference:\n\n1. **Move the price-dependent assertions off the fork** (fix #2 above). Mocked + fuzzed tests need\n   no RPC at all. This removes the archive requirement for exactly the three tests that broke, and\n   it's the change you should make regardless.\n2. **Get a free archive endpoint.** Several providers include archive access on their free tier —\n   verify with the `cast` checks above rather than trusting the pricing page. Keep the paid-shaped\n   URL in CI secrets; nothing else changes.\n3. **Commit the warm cache.** Populate `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/<FORK_BLOCK>/` once from a\n   machine that does have archive access, commit it, point CI at it. CI then makes zero RPC calls\n   and is fully deterministic. Caveats: repo bloat, and a cache *miss* silently falls through to the\n   network — so add a CI assertion that the suite makes no outbound RPC calls, or you'll drift back\n   into today's situation without noticing.\n4. **Last resort — pin to a recent block within the ~128-block window.** Works on a full node, but\n   the pin expires within the hour, so it only buys determinism *within* a run. Not a fix.\n\n## Summary\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fixed by |\n|---|---|---|\n| Sudden reds | Assertions on live market data | Pin block; mock+fuzz for price logic |\n| Flaky re-runs | Different head per run/contract; 429 retry exhaustion | Pin block |\n| Steady slowdown | Cache keyed by block → 100% miss rate | Pin block + cache `~/.foundry/cache/rpc` in CI |\n| HTTP 429s | Uncached call volume grew past free-tier limit | Same cache; throttle the cold run |\n\nThe one-line version: `vm.createSelectFork(url)` without a block number is not a fork test, it's a\nmainnet monitoring alarm wired into your PR gate. Pin the block, cache the responses, and stop\nasserting on numbers the market owns.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":587,"cache_read_input_tokens":27618,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":587},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8df734a9-bd87-4a12-8378-0091c8af4975","uuid":"fecd1414-bd85-4d5d-985a-1c82b1b91b42","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:16:05.320Z","request_id":"req_011CdSEADEFY4yoQgq2Rcx1J"}
{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012uuHwanR2chj3bpkcYRZPE","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081344Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"8df734a9-bd87-4a12-8378-0091c8af4975","uuid":"fb5eb796-501d-4c02-99ab-4f4ca4bc3add","timestamp":"2026-07-27T08:16:05.348Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"create","filePath":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/testing-quiz-004/2026-07-27T081344Z-claude-with-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Why all four symptoms are the same bug\n\n## The root cause\n\n```solidity\nvm.createSelectFork(vm.envString(\"MAINNET_RPC_URL\"));\n```\n\nNo block number. That overload forks at **`latest`**. Every CI run — every test contract inside\na run — forks a different block of a chain that never stops moving.\n\nSo the suite has no fixed input. The Chainlink answer and the Uniswap reserves your assertions\ncompare against are not constants you're testing; they're live market data you're re-downloading\neach run. All four symptoms fall out of that one line.\n\n## How each symptom follows\n\n**1. The sudden reds.** Nothing in your repo changed. Mainnet changed. A Chainlink aggregator only\nwrites a new answer when price deviates past its threshold (~0.5% for ETH/USD) or its heartbeat\nexpires — so an asserted price can sit inside a hardcoded band for months and then step outside it\nin one round. Uniswap reserves move on every swap and every LP mint/burn, so any tolerance you\npicked drifts out as liquidity changes. Three tests turned red this morning because the market\ncrossed your thresholds this morning.\n\nThe important consequence: **the four-month green streak was never evidence these tests passed.**\nIt was evidence the market happened to stay in range. The tests have been broken since they were\nwritten; today is just when it surfaced.\n\n**2. The flakiness on re-run.** Same commit, different head. A re-run 10 minutes later forks a\ndifferent block, where the price may be back inside the band or the Chainlink round hasn't rotated\nyet. Two channels feed this:\n\n- *State drift* — the block you land on decides pass/fail.\n- *Failed RPC calls* — see (4). A request that exhausts Foundry's retries surfaces as a test error,\n  not as a network error, so it reads as a flaky failure.\n\nThere's also intra-run inconsistency: `forge test` runs test **contracts** in parallel, each with\nits own `setUp`, so each resolves `latest` independently and they can land on different blocks\nwithin a single invocation. You cannot assume all your tests saw the same chain state even in one\nrun.\n\n**3. The slowdown.** Foundry caches fork RPC responses on disk, keyed by **chain + block number**\n(`~/.foundry/cache/rpc/<chain>/<block>/`). A moving head means a new key every run, so the hit rate\nis **zero, permanently**. Every `SLOAD`, `eth_getCode`, and `eth_call` your tests touch is a live\nnetwork round trip, every time. As you added tests over four months, the per-run RPC call count grew\nmonotonically and none of it was ever amortized. The cache directory grew too — pure disk bloat, no\nreuse.\n\n**4. The 429s.** Direct consequence of (3). Uncached calls per run × parallel test contracts finally\ncrossed your free tier's rate / compute-unit ceiling. And this feeds back: 429 → Foundry backs off\nand retries → longer wall time (worse slowdown) → exhausted retries → test error (more flakiness).\n\nOne line, four symptoms, with a reinforcing loop between the last two.\n\n## The fix\n\n### 1. Pin the block\n\n```toml\n# foundry.toml\n[rpc_endpoints]\nmainnet = \"${MAINNET_RPC_URL}\"\n\n[rpc_storage_caching]\nchains    = [\"mainnet\"]\nendpoints = \"all\"\n```\n\n```solidity\ncontract ForkTest is Test {\n    // Bump deliberately, in its own PR. Never \"latest\".\n    uint256 constant FORK_BLOCK = 19_000_000;\n\n    function setUp() public {\n        vm.createSelectFork(\"mainnet\", FORK_BLOCK);\n    }\n}\n```\n\nNow the Chainlink answer and the pool reserves at that block are *constants*. Assert exact values,\nnot tolerance bands — a band is just a slower way to be non-deterministic:\n\n```solidity\nfunction test_ChainlinkPriceAtForkBlock() public view {\n    (, int256 answer,,,) = AggregatorV3Interface(ETH_USD_FEED).latestRoundData();\n    assertEq(answer, 224_351_000_000); // read once at FORK_BLOCK, then frozen\n}\n```\n\nTreat the pin like a lockfile: bumping it is a reviewed change, and if a protocol upgrade breaks\nyou, the diff says so instead of a random Tuesday saying so.\n\n### 2. Split what these tests are actually for\n\nPinning fixes determinism but doesn't fix the design problem: two different questions are being\nanswered by one test.\n\n- *\"Does our integration wire up against the real deployed contracts?\"* → pinned fork test. Correct\n  use, keep it.\n- *\"Does our logic behave correctly across price ranges?\"* → **don't fork at all.** Mock the feed\n  and fuzz the price. A market move should be incapable of turning CI red.\n\n```solidity\nfunction testFuzz_HandlesAnyPrice(int256 price) public {\n    price = int256(bound(uint256(price), 1e8, 100_000e8));\n    vm.mockCall(\n        ETH_USD_FEED,\n        abi.encodeWithSelector(AggregatorV3Interface.latestRoundData.selector),\n        abi.encode(uint80(1), price, block.timestamp, block.timestamp, uint80(1))\n    );\n    // ... assert your logic, no network involved\n}\n```\n\nThis is also where you should be testing the cases a live fork will basically never hand you:\nstale rounds, a zero or negative answer, a price that moved 40% between two calls.\n\n### 3. Cache the RPC responses in CI\n\nOnce the block is pinned the cache is reusable, so make CI keep it:\n\n```yaml\n- uses: actions/cache@v4\n  with:\n    path: ~/.foundry/cache/rpc\n    key: foundry-rpc-${{ env.FORK_BLOCK }}-${{ hashFiles('test/**/*.sol') }}\n    restore-keys: foundry-rpc-${{ env.FORK_BLOCK }}-\n```\n\nAfter the first warm run, a normal PR makes close to zero RPC calls. That is what actually kills the\n429s and the slowdown — pinning alone only makes the cache *possible*.\n\n### 4. Survive the cold run\n\nThe first run at a new pin still downloads state, in a burst, in parallel. Throttle it:\n\n```bash\nforge test --compute-units-per-second 100   # or --no-rpc-rate-limit if you have headroom\n```\n\n## Does this work against a free-tier endpoint? — plainly\n\n**Pinning to a block older than ~128 blocks requires archive state, and the fix does not work\nwithout it.** That is the one thing your endpoint may not provide.\n\nA full (non-archive) node prunes historical world state after ~128 blocks (~25 minutes). Fork\ntesting at `FORK_BLOCK` needs historical `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getCode`, and\n`eth_call` **at that block**. Outside the window, a non-archive node cannot answer.\n\nFree tiers vary and terms change, so don't take anyone's word for it — including mine. Check yours:\n\n```bash\n# 1. historical state read\ncast balance 0xd8dA6BF26964aF9D7eEd9e03E53415D37aA96045 \\\n  --block 19000000 --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\"\n\n# 2. historical eth_call — what fork tests actually need\ncast call 0x5f4eC3Df9cbd43714FE2740f5E3616155c5b8419 \"latestAnswer()(int256)\" \\\n  --block 19000000 --rpc-url \"$MAINNET_RPC_URL\"\n```\n\n- Both return values → you have archive at that depth. Ship the fix as written.\n- Either errors with `missing trie node`, `state is not available`,\n  `Historical state not available`, or a bare `-32000` → **no archive**. Note that some providers\n  serve archive but only for a limited lookback, so run the check against the exact block you plan\n  to pin, not an arbitrary old one.\n\nAlso check the ceiling, not just capability: free tiers cap requests/sec and monthly compute units.\nArchive calls are usually billed at a higher weight. A cold run at a fresh pin can burn a\nmeaningful chunk of a monthly free quota in one go.\n\n### If you don't have archive\n\nIn rough order of preference:\n\n1. **Move the price-dependent assertions off the fork** (fix #2 above). Mocked + fuzzed tests need\n   no RPC at all. This removes the archive requirement for exactly the three tests that broke, and\n   it's the change you should make regardless.\n2. **Get a free archive endpoint.** Several providers include archive access on their free tier —\n   verify with the `cast` checks above rather than trusting the pricing page. Keep the paid-shaped\n   URL in CI secrets; nothing else changes.\n3. **Commit the warm cache.** Populate `~/.foundry/cache/rpc/mainnet/<FORK_BLOCK>/` once from a\n   machine that does have archive access, commit it, point CI at it. CI then makes zero RPC calls\n   and is fully deterministic. Caveats: repo bloat, and a cache *miss* silently falls through to the\n   network — so add a CI assertion that the suite makes no outbound RPC calls, or you'll drift back\n   into today's situation without noticing.\n4. **Last resort — pin to a recent block within the ~128-block window.** Works on a full node, but\n   the pin expires within the hour, so it only buys determinism *within* a run. Not a fix.\n\n## Summary\n\n| Symptom | Cause | Fixed by |\n|---|---|---|\n| Sudden reds | Assertions on live market data | Pin block; mock+fuzz for price logic |\n| Flaky re-runs | Different head per run/contract; 429 retry exhaustion | Pin block |\n| Steady slowdown | Cache keyed by block → 100% miss rate | Pin block + cache `~/.foundry/cache/rpc` in CI |\n| HTTP 429s | Uncached call volume grew past free-tier limit | Same cache; throttle the cold run |\n\nThe one-line version: `vm.createSelectFork(url)` without a block number is not a fork test, it's a\nmainnet monitoring alarm wired into your PR gate. Pin the block, cache the responses, and stop\nasserting on numbers the market owns.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
